# libertty +pick and +input: a script's question over the window of the pane
# it runs in, as a page of the palette, and the answer printed — an item, any
# number of them, what's typed; Esc exits 1 printing nothing, out of time
# 124, a second question while one is up 5; the question goes when its
# command does. Run with --persist (the pane is found by its session).
type:R=$(libertty +pick --title Branch main dev feature); echo "PICKED=[$R] EXIT=$?"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Branch | From Tab 1 · libertty-ui-probe
expect-prompt:| main | dev | feature
type-then:enter:dev
wait:1.0
expect-prompt:none
expect:PICKED=[dev] EXIT=0
# Items on stdin, each with its detail (shown, not printed).
type:R=$(printf 'one\tfirst\ntwo\tsecond\n' | libertty +pick --title Number); echo "STDIN=[$R]"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Number
expect-prompt:| one | two
type-then:enter:two
wait:1.0
expect:STDIN=[two]
# Any number: Tab marks one and goes on; Return answers with the marked ones, in the list's order.
type:R=$(libertty +pick --multiple apple banana cherry | tr '\n' ,); echo "MULTI=[$R]"
key:enter
wait:1.5
key:tab
key:down
key:tab
expect-prompt:| ✓ apple | banana | ✓ cherry
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect:MULTI=[apple,cherry,]
# Or an answer of your own.
type:R=$(libertty +pick --allow-other red green); echo "OTHER=[$R]"
key:enter
wait:1.5
type-then:enter:blue
wait:1.0
expect:OTHER=[blue]
# A line typed over what it starts with.
type:R=$(libertty +input --title Name --value hello); echo "INPUT=[$R] EXIT=$?"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Name | From Tab 1
expect-prompt:[hello]
type-then:enter:world
wait:1.0
expect:INPUT=[world] EXIT=0
# A secret: its answer comes back in a private file of the command's, not
# in the reply, and the file is gone after.
type:R=$(libertty +input --title Token --secure); echo "SECRET=[$R] EXIT=$? LEFT=$(ls -d ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/libertty-answer.* 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Token
type-then:enter:s3cr3t
wait:1.0
expect:SECRET=[s3cr3t] EXIT=0 LEFT=0
# Esc: 1, nothing printed.
type:R=$(libertty +input --title Never); echo "CANCEL=[$R] $?"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Never
key:escape
wait:1.0
expect-prompt:none
expect:CANCEL=[] 1
# Out of time: 124, and the question goes by itself.
type:libertty +pick --timeout 1 x y; echo "TIMEOUT=$?"
key:enter
wait:3.0
expect-prompt:none
expect:TIMEOUT=124
# One at a time: a second one while the first is up is turned away (5).
type:libertty +pick --title First a b & sleep 1.5; libertty +pick c d; echo "BUSY=$?"
key:enter
wait:3.5
expect:BUSY=5
expect-prompt:First
key:escape
wait:1.0
expect-prompt:none
# Its command killed: the question goes with it.
type:libertty +pick --title Killed a b & sleep 3; kill $!; wait $!; echo "KILLED=$?"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Killed
wait:2.5
expect:KILLED=143
expect-prompt:none
# Its pane closed (its program still running, kept for Undo): the question
# goes, and the command hears why.
type:libertty +split --no-focus -e 'libertty +pick --title Split a b 2> why; echo "CODE=$?" > code; sleep 60' > /dev/null
key:enter
wait:2.5
expect-prompt:Split
expect-panes:2
action:goto_split:next
action:close_surface
wait:1.5
expect-panes:1
expect-prompt:none
type:cat code why
key:enter
wait:0.8
expect:CODE=1
expect:its pane closed
# Outside a Libertty pane: over the window in front, nobody named as asking.
type:R=$(env -u LIBERTTY_SESSION libertty +pick --title Front q w); echo "FRONT=[$R]"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-prompt:Front | [] | q | w
type-then:enter:w
wait:1.0
expect:FRONT=[w]
# What's wrong with a command line is said, and nothing is asked.
type:libertty +pick --multiple --allow-other a; echo "USAGE=$?"
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect:USAGE=2
expect:don't go together
expect-prompt:none
